messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: line numbers in error messages
parts:
I think Bob mentioned that it would be good to have exceptions and other errors associate themselves with the line number in the code.

Apparently, this is easy with the __FILE__ and __LINE__ preprocessor macros, both of which seem to be supported by g++ and clang++; see

http://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/cpp/Standard-Predefined-Macros.html

or

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/tmp$ cat test.cpp
#include<fstream>

int main() {
     fprintf (stderr, "Internal error: "
                      "look at "
                      "%s, line %d.\n",
              __FILE__, __LINE__);

    return 0;
}
goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/tmp$ clang++ test.cpp
goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/tmp$ ./a.out
Internal error: look at test.cpp, line 7.


Ben

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] line numbers in error messages
parts:
This is nice for C++ error messages, but it won't help end users track down errors in their models without diving into the C++ which is what Bob and I had talked about a bit a while back.  There is actually a straightforward way to do it, provided we could get the model file line numbers and line contents in the right part of the output but that involves some parser magic that has yet to be sorted out.

Cheers,
Marcus
